record_type_quote: The current study investigated math anxiety of elementary school teachers to replicate the higher levels of math anxiety found for teachers as compared to a reference sample, to identify which teachers are affected, and to disclose how math anxiety relates to their teaching attitudes.

targets.title: Preservice to inservice: Does mathematics anxiety change with teaching experience?
targets.evidence_quote: Consistent with this reported decrease in math anxiety during teacher education, Gresham (2018) found evidence for a further decrease in math anxiety when teachers start teaching. Our study, however, does not support these previously found differences and instead provides moderate evidence for similar levels of math anxiety for female pre-service and in-service elementary school teachers, even when specialization in math was taken into account.

reasoning: Assigned PsychArchives DOI identifies the accepted manuscript and its landing page explicitly links the same article version of record. The complete version of record, with matching title and all five authors, was obtained from its author repository after the assigned manuscript download returned 502. Primary originals whose specific findings are re-tested in the stated main and secondary aims are coded separately, including conceptual comparisons of teaching attitudes with confidence, efficacy and teaching anxiety. Those secondary target relationships are broader than the main replication and this uncertainty is recorded here; outcome confidence concerns the authors’ explicit comparisons. Hembree (1990) is the named meta-analytic motivation, but the primary studies are retained rather than treating a meta-analysis as a primary original. Turkish prevalence studies are contextual country comparisons; within-training changes are not the same contrast as pre-service versus in-service experience, so those are not targets. Child achievement and intervention findings were not tested. No original study numbers are specified.
